entries.title: init writes hooks that run the install you ran, not the first one on PATH
entries.summary: `init` wrote every hook, the Codex server entry and the post-upgrade hook refresh with the first `jcodemunch-mcp` on PATH, so running a newer install's `init` from a venv or a `uv tool` environment, with an older install on PATH, gave hooks that call the older version. They now name the install that ran. Under `uvx`, whose cache `uv cache clean` deletes, `init` writes the next install on PATH and prints which, with the command that makes the hooks call the version you ran.

entries.title: a package named migrations is indexed, and the start-up instructions stop preferring the index everywhere
entries.summary: `migrations` was on the built-in skip list, so a library whose own code lives in a package of that name, such as django's migration framework, never entered the index. A `migrations` directory is now skipped only when it holds files named the way a migration tool names what it writes (`0001_initial.py`, `V1__init.sql`, a timestamp), and the skip is counted as `generated_migrations`. The `instructions` string the server sends at session start no longer tells agents to prefer the index over Read and Grep or to call `resolve_repo` first; it says what the agent policy says: the index for relationships, a large repository or an open question, and the built-in tools for a known name in a small one.

entries.title: an installed agent policy can be brought up to date, and only when you ask
entries.summary: `init` writes the agent policy into CLAUDE.md once and never rewrites it, so the policy rewritten in 1.108.357 reached new installs only. `jcodemunch-mcp claude-md --refresh` replaces an installed block that differs: it shows the diff, asks before writing (`--yes` skips the question, `--dry-run` writes nothing), keeps a timestamped backup and changes nothing outside the block. The first `resolve_repo` answer of an existing install says once, for each policy text, that the command exists, and asks the agent to tell you rather than run it. SECURITY.md lists what the server reads for this and the marker it writes. Also from @outoftheblue9 (#1075): a C# or AL symbol documented with `///` comments is summarised by its sentence, not by the literal `<summary>` tag, which also improves search on those codebases. Indexes re-parse on their next run (parser generation 21).

entries.title: a Web Forms attribute is read in every form ASP.NET accepts, and a schema stays capped in every repository
entries.summary: From @outoftheblue9 (#1067). The Web Forms reader took only double-quoted attribute values, so an unquoted `runat=server` or a single-quoted `CodeFile='Q.aspx.cs'` gave a control's handler no reference and a page no edge to its codebehind; live code could read as unused. Directives, `runat`, `ID`, `On*` handlers and `<script runat>` are now read double-quoted, single-quoted and unquoted, in one pass that takes each quoted value whole. `.xsd` and `.wsdl` files stay capped in every repository: `build_consumed` with project-file advice where the index holds .NET evidence, and the new neutral kind `schema_consumer` (counted as `schema_consumer_withheld`) elsewhere, so a Java repository no longer gets .NET advice. Indexes re-parse on their next run (parser generation 20).
